extract:
Jean-Guihen Queyras is a French cellist, born in Montreal in 1967 and raised in Algeria and then in Provence, in the south of France. He has been one of the most versatile cellists of his generation since the early 1990s. His career spans the Baroque repertoire, the Classical and Romantic canon, and contemporary music. That breadth was shaped by his formative years in a decisive way.

Queyras studied in Lyon and later in Germany and the United States. His career took shape when Pierre Boulez appointed him principal cellist of the Ensemble Intercontemporain in Paris, a post he held from 1990 to 2001. That decade immersed him in modern repertoire and close collaboration with living composers. It is reflected in his early discography, including the Deutsche Grammophon recording of Ligeti's Cello, Violin and Piano Concertos with Boulez and the Ensemble Intercontemporain. He also took part in recordings of Ivan Fedele's music and Luigi Dallapiccola's orchestral works.

After leaving the ensemble, Queyras built a solo and chamber career, largely through a long association with the French label harmonia mundi. His recording of Haydn's Cello Concertos Nos. 1 and 2, paired with Georg Matthias Monn's concerto, was made with the Freiburger Baroque Orchestra under Petra Müllejans. It showed his fluency in period-informed style. His Dvořák Cello Concerto with the Prague Philharmonia under Jiří Bělohlávek was coupled with the "Dumky" Trio, recorded with violinist Isabelle Faust and pianist Alexander Melnikov. His 2007 recording of Bach's complete Cello Suites became a reference version, praised for its dance-like lightness and rhetorical clarity. Further harmonia mundi releases included Schubert's Arpeggione Sonata alongside Berg and Webern, and Debussy and Poulenc sonatas with pianist Alexandre Tharaud. These programs typify his habit of placing older and modern works side by side.

His chamber partnerships are central to his identity. With Isabelle Faust and Alexander Melnikov he formed a celebrated trio, recording Beethoven trios among other works. With Tharaud he developed a long-standing duo. He was also a founding member of the Arcanto Quartet, alongside Antje Weithaas, Daniel Sepec and Tabea Zimmermann. He has kept close ties with composers, premiering or championing works by figures such as Philippe Schoeller and Bruno Mantovani.

Critics have consistently singled out his technical poise, warmth of tone and stylistic intelligence. His recordings have received honours including Gramophone awards and Diapasons d'Or. His Bach Suites in particular are often cited among the finest modern versions. Beyond the concert hall, he has explored crossover projects with Iranian zarb players Keyvan and Bijan Chemirani, drawing on Mediterranean and Persian traditions.

Queyras continues to perform internationally as a soloist and chamber musician and records regularly for harmonia mundi. He teaches at the Musikhochschule in Freiburg and has served as artistic director of the Rencontres Musicales de Haute-Provence festival in Forcalquier. His legacy rests on uniting the rigour of the Boulez-era avant-garde with deep engagement in historical performance.
title: Jean-Guihen Queyras
